# FDG4062

> CONSIDER using the format `<V>.<S>.<B>.<R>` for the assembly file version, where `V` is the major version number, `S` is the servicing number, `B` is the build number, and `R` is the build revision number.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.10 Types and Assembly Metadata.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG4062
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Use the format <V>.<S>.<B>.<R> for the assembly file version '{0}'

Library only: the file version informs the users of an assembly. FDG4062 reports a hand-written AssemblyFileVersionAttribute whose value is not four dot-separated numbers; what each number means is not checked. The attribute that SDK-style projects generate is generated code and is not reported.

## From the book

For example, this is how the version attribute is applied in `System.Core.dll`, which shipped as part of .NET Framework 3.5:

```csharp
[assembly:AssemblyFileVersion("3.5.21022.8")]
```
